reason: The case needs a file endpoint and a storage the stack does not have. The design names POST /api/v1/files/{id}/download-url, and openapi.json has no operation of that kind: the signed links of the stack are the ones of each feature (exports, document versions), signed and checked by the API itself (apps/api/src/modules/files/file.service.ts over FsObjectStorage, a file-system mock), so an expired link is answered 401 SIGNATURE_INVALID by the API, never 403 by a storage service. The 300 seconds of the link are one constant of the kernel with a clock the stack cannot move, so the case would wait 301 real seconds on a mock that is not the storage the design means. The EICAR upload is scanned by MockScanPort, an upload of an infected file is refused with 422 FILE_NOT_CLEAN by the upload route and no FileObject record with scan_status=INFECTED is written; the 'attach to a report' command of the design does not exist. What the stack can show (a file of tenant B is 404 for tenant A; a link signed for B is refused) is only a part of the case, and a part is not the case.
needs: An object storage with signed URLs that expires them by its own clock and answers 403 by itself (S3 compatible, or MinIO), a real antivirus scanner (ClamAV) behind the ScanPort, the generic file endpoint POST /files/{id}/download-url and a FileObject record with scan_status in the API, and an attach command that answers 422 VALIDATION_FAILED for an infected file.

reason: The case needs a Temporal test server and a way to put a task of a queue with a changed payload. The stack has no Temporal: its workflows run in the in-process orchestrator (apps/api/src/modules/orchestration/in-process-orchestrator.ts), which verifies the signed TenantContext of every start, signal and describe (TENANT_CONTEXT_INVALID, covered by jest tests in apps/api/test/orchestration and apps/api/test/cap/plan-approval-workflow.test.ts), but no HTTP route lets a caller hand it an activity payload with a changed tenant_id and an old signature, and no workflow history, no 'SET LOCAL' log of a worker and no security alert (the audit_event row with an action like '%tenant_context%' that the case asserts) is observable from the stack. A forged bearer token at the HTTP door is a different check (the authentication guard) and does not prove that a task of the queue is refused.
needs: A Temporal test server with the ApprovalWorkflow worker of tenant A (CAP-PLAN-A-01), a client that can enqueue an activity task with an edited tenant_id and the old signature, the workflow history and the database log of the worker, and the security alert that the design says is emitted (the code that writes it does not exist in apps/api/src: nothing writes an audit action with 'tenant_context').
